title: Tensor decomposition over an etale localization
statement: Let $A\to C$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $C$ is free over $A$ with a finite basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Let $h\in C$, put $B=C_h$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and assume that $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Form the commutative algebra $T=C\otimes_A B$ [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], regarded as a $B$-algebra through the second factor, and let $\mu:T\to B$ be the $B$-algebra map $c\otimes b\mapsto\bar c b$, where $\bar c$ is the image of $c$ in $B$. There exist a commutative $B$-algebra $D$ and an isomorphism of $B$-algebras $\theta:T\xrightarrow{\sim}B\times D$ such that $\operatorname{pr}_1\circ\theta=\mu$.

source.place: Tag 0812 (lemma-trick-fitting-ideal), proof: the multiplication map C tensor_A C_h to C_h is etale and flat; Tag 00U8 (algebra.tex, lemma-surjective-flat-finitely-presented), applied there after Tag 00U7 (lemma-map-between-etale), gives the displayed product decomposition.

proof.text: Write $\lambda:C\to B$ for localization and $i:C\to T$, $j:B\to T$ for $c\mapsto c\otimes1$, $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. The tensor pushout universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property](2) applied to $\lambda$ and $\mathrm{id}_B$ gives $\mu(c\otimes b)=\lambda(c)b$. It gives $\mu i=\lambda$ and $\mu j=\mathrm{id}_B$. In particular $\mu$ is surjective, and it is a $B$-algebra map for the second-factor structure $j$.

source.place: Tag 0812 (lemma-trick-fitting-ideal), proof: the multiplication map is a section; tensor formulas expanded

proof.text: Translate the assumed spectrum-etaleness to Algebra.Etale A B using HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff and RingHom.etale_algebraMap. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change], T is etale over C. The principal localization C to B is etale, the consequence of [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] and clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]; Lean applies the direct ring theorem Algebra.Etale.of_isLocalizationAway. Give B the T-algebra structure induced by mu. The tensor formula mu(c tensor 1) = lambda(c) supplies the scalar tower C to T to B. Apply Algebra.Etale.of_restrictScalars C T B, the ring form of clause (3) of the cancellation node. Thus the surjective map mu is etale; no etaleness of T over B is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0812 proof, etaleness of the multiplication map; Algebra Tag 00U7 (lemma-map-between-etale), with base change 00U2 and principal localization 01I3

proof.text: Put I = ker(mu). Steps 1–2 verify the surjectivity and etaleness assumptions of [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-etale-kernel-idempotent-fg]. Apply Algebra.FormallyEtale.iff_of_surjective to get I*I = I, and Algebra.FinitePresentation.ker_fG_of_surjective over T to get finite generation. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fg-idempotent-ideal-idempotent-generator](1), implemented by Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg, to obtain an idempotent e in T with I = (e).

Put D = T/(1-e), a quotient commutative B-algebra using the second-factor B-algebra structure on T. Since e and 1-e are idempotent, sum to 1, and have product zero, the complementary-idempotent quotient theorem AlgEquiv.prodQuotientOfIsIdempotentElem gives a B-algebra equivalence theta_1 : T to T/(e) times T/(1-e). Its projections are the two quotient maps. This uses the same complementary-idempotent identities as the corner-ring construction, with the quotient model for the complementary factor.

source.place: Tag 0812 proof, product splitting from 00U8; elementary complementary-idempotent product map written out

proof.text: The equality ker(mu) = (e) identifies T/(e) with T/ker(mu). Surjectivity of mu and the first isomorphism theorem Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective identify the latter with B as a B-algebra. Compose theta_1 with the product of this equivalence and the identity on D. On t the first projection is the kernel quotient lift evaluated on the quotient class of t, which is mu(t) by RingHom.kerLift_mk. This gives the requested equivalence and its prescribed first projection.

lean.statement: theorem exists_etaleLocalization_tensor_splitting (A C : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] [Module.Free A C] [Module.Finite A C] (h : C) [AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (Localization.Away h))))] : ∃ (D : Type u) (_ : CommRing D) (_ : Algebra (Localization.Away h) D) (θ : @AlgEquiv (Localization.Away h) (C ⊗[A] Localization.Away h) (Localization.Away h × D) _ _ _ (Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := A) (A := C) (B := Localization.Away h)) _), ∀ t : C ⊗[A] Localization.Away h, (θ t).1 = Algebra.TensorProduct.productMap (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom A C (Localization.Away h)) (AlgHom.id A (Localization.Away h)) t
